A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same SandboxVLM method and core experiments. v2 ends after the references; v3 includes additional supplementary material. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1-3 report original SandboxVLM benchmark evaluations, backbone comparisons, and representation ablations.

after.justification: Retains the original experiments and adds a single-image ablation, human-verified error statistics, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.5 retain the same generation, proxy elevation, voting, clustering, box rendering, and reasoning pipeline. Newly documented implementation details do not establish a procedural change; Single Image Sandbox is an ablation of the retained full method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate SAT-Real, SAT-Synth, BLINK spatial/depth tasks, EmbSpatial, and PhysBench. The supplementary benchmark examples and failure cases elaborate existing coverage rather than introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Single Image Sandbox as a comparator without generated multi-view priors. The external baseline sets in Tables 1-2 and the other ablation comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added ablation introduces a control that removes video generation under the retained SAT-Real/GPT-5-mini evaluation. v3 also introduces human verification for the error analysis, labeled as 318 cases in Figure 5. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; newly disclosed sampling details do not establish changed sampling.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing representation ablations, v3 directly tests the contribution of generated views and adds a module-level error breakdown plus representation-specific failure cases in Sections 7-8 and Figures 5-6. This substantially expands diagnosis of the pipeline's weaknesses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new error-category frequencies are descriptive results, without an added uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 and matched Table 3 rows retain identical values. v3 adds Single Image Sandbox at 77.6% versus the retained full model's 84.1%, and Figure 5 error frequencies. The introductory SAT gain changes from 7.2% to 3.8%, matching Table 1's 84.1 versus 80.3.

T1.justification: The task definition and Equations (1)-(8) remain substantively unchanged. Abbreviating 'forward' to 'fwd' does not alter the mathematics. No new proofs, formal assumptions, or theoretical results appear.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the claim that boxes encode physical kinematics, and the introduction/conclusion emphasize spatial rather than broader physical or multimodal intelligence. The conclusion changes 'often sufficient' to 'sometimes sufficient.' The central training-free abstract-perception contribution remains.

C2.justification: Sections 7-8 add explanations of pointing/segmentation error propagation, connect object-movement weaknesses to static reconstruction, and identify missing facing-direction details as a failure condition. Existing limitations concerning dynamic scenes and unmodeled physical properties remain.

D1.justification: The new supplement supplies API dates, motion parameters, generation settings, the reasoning prompt, and 98 SAT-Synth sample indices, previously unavailable in v2. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation, although Section 6.1 inconsistently specifies both N=3 and N=2 for multi-view voting.

R1.justification: Related work revises descriptions of 3D-LLM, MiniGPT-3D, and ShapeLLM, adds Armeni et al.'s 3D Scene Graph, and removes Omni-ShapeLLM and several other citations. The overall positioning against supervised 3D models remains; bibliographic corrections alone are not treated as new works.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract and conclusion, rewrites part of related work, shortens the backbone discussion, and adds contact information and acknowledgements. Supplementary sections organize the additional material, while the main document's section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual presentation with module-failure panels and an error chart in Figure 5, annotated reasoning failures in Figure 6, and benchmark-example and component-comparison Tables 4-5. Table 3 gains an ablation row; the original main figures and table layouts remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: The new single-image control strengthens evidence for generated views, while supplementary prompts, sample indices, and failure analyses improve transparency. Narrower claims better reflect the geometric representation. However, conflicting voting parameters in Section 6.1 and Table 5's omission of the new ablation limit the gains. The overall improvement is modest, with the main method and benchmark results unchanged.
